adds.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Federal placement mechanics that govern trans prisoners in federal custody inside Alberta: since 2018, federal corrections operations accommodate offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth, and the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement or transfer to a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression, regardless of anatomy or the sex/gender marker on identity documents, with requests refused only where CSC finds unresolvable 'overriding health or safety concerns'. As of 2025 CSC reported 90 self-identified transgender women in federal institutions - 73 housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator called CSC's 2022 gender-diversity policy an important change but flagged the lack of clear parameters for what counts as an 'overriding health or safety concern' and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary and the article documents no Alberta-specific rule.

adds.title: Danielle Smith (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia biography of Alberta Premier Danielle Smith records her 12 February 2024 announcement of the province's package of trans-restricting measures (ban on gender-affirming care for minors, parental-consent rules for school pronouns and sexuality instruction, ban on trans women in women's sports), and that the bans 'would not include a ban on women's shelters, women's prisons or women's changing rooms', citing CBC's Lily Dupuis (12 April 2024) that Alberta's proposed transgender rules won't include public change rooms or jails. Outcome for the prison axis: Alberta's statutory trans package deliberately excluded jail and prison settings, so no provincial placement-by-birth-sex rule for trans prisoners was enacted, and no Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement, special unit, or segregation case is documented.

records.note: No Alberta-specific trans-prisoner housing rule was found: the mandated single enwiki full-text search (query 'Alberta prison transgender') returned nothing province-specific, and the two candidate fetches show (a) the federal Correctional Service of Canada identity-based placement policy (2018+, identity-aligned institution on request absent unresolvable safety concerns; as of 2025, 73 of 90 federal trans women housed in men's institutions) governs federal inmates held in Alberta, and (b) Alberta's 2024-25 trans statutes explicitly excluded jails and women's prisons from their scope (CBC, 12 Apr 2024), so no birth-sex placement statute, no trans special unit, and no documented solitary/segregation practice or ruling for trans prisoners in Alberta was located within the fetch budget.

adds.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Federal placement policy applicable to trans prisoners in federal custody inside Saskatchewan: since 2018 the Correctional Service of Canada accommodates offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth and permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement in a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression regardless of anatomy or identity-document sex/gender marker, refusing requests individually only where 'overriding health or safety concerns' cannot be resolved; as of 2025, of 90 self-identified transgender women in federal custody, 73 were housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator (2022-23 report) welcomed the 2022 gender-diversity policy but flagged unclear override parameters and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary (the article's only provincial example is Ontario) and no Saskatchewan-specific rule or case is documented in this source.

records.note: No Saskatchewan-specific trans-prisoner housing data was found: the mandated single enwiki full-text search (query 'Saskatchewan prison transgender') returned no province-specific placement content or case - top hits were generic Canada-level articles and 'Everett Klippert', a 1960s preventive-detention case over same-sex conduct rather than trans placement - and the candidate fetches ('Transgender rights in Canada'; 'LGBTQ rights in Canada') document only the federal Correctional Service of Canada identity-based placement policy governing federal inmates held in Saskatchewan. No Saskatchewan birth-sex-vs-identity provincial placement rule, no trans special unit, and no solitary/segregation practice or ruling for trans prisoners was located within the fetch budget; thin finding, no fabrication.
